captions.text: In Core, open Routes and find the Community supply loop.
Select Directions on that plan’s row.
This fictional two-stop supply exercise helps a coordinator review the
proposed roads before assigning work.
The directions are provider estimates for the saved locations.
They do not show a vehicle journey or prove that a road
is suitable for your vehicle.

scenes.title: Review the whole loop and its estimates

captions.text: The Directions page draws the planned loop and displays twelve point seven
kilometres, thirty-one minutes, and fifty-six minutes in parentheses.
The longer total includes the planned stop dwell times.
Review the map and the intended stop locations together.
Start Route is available here, but opening this page alone has
not started a new execution.
Scroll to Turn-by-Turn Directions.
Supply point A has its own leg distance and duration, followed
by the individual turns.
Further down, Community point B has a separate leg.
The final Firehouse fifty-one section is the return leg to the station.
Read the road names and distances in the relevant section, rather than assuming
the overall duration describes every leg.

scenes.title: Check the stop work and planned dwell

captions.text: Stop Summary brings the saved stop names, addresses, Dwell,
Contact and Notes together.
This example plans ten minutes at Supply point A and fifteen at Community point B.
These are planning values, not measured check-in durations.
Check the notes with the crew before beginning.
A search-and-rescue supply run, community paramedicine route,
security round, wildland support task or industrial response assignment
can use the same planning pattern.

scenes.title: Review the Unit preview before starting

captions.text: In Unit, View Route shows the same saved plan with two stops, twelve point
seven kilometres and thirty-one minutes.
Review those details before selecting Start Route.
Route planning and the active unit execution are separate states.
Start Route begins the unit assignment; the route plan remains reusable.

scenes.title: Open guidance from the active execution

captions.text: On Active Route, review Current Step and select Directions.
The returned Directions view shows its own road line, Distance, Duration and E T A.
Here it connects Supply point A to Community point B and shows five hundred
eighty-three metres and two minutes.
This is a shorter scope than the complete station-to-stops-and-return
loop shown in Core.
Read the endpoints before comparing the totals.
No traffic data is shown, and location is unavailable in this software exercise.
Open in Maps is available for an external map handoff; that handoff
is not performed in this recording.
